<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__PageHeaderProps__breadcrumb.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in isTombstoneIssue))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in isTombstoneIssue))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in isTombstoneIssue))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in isTombstoneIssue))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in isTombstoneIssue))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in isTombstoneIssue), invalid_union (literal, a string literal in isRetiredKeyVerdict))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via PageHeaderProps (symbol, a top-level const object), invalid_type (literal, a string literal in isTombstoneIssue))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__PageHeaderProps__breadcrumb.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dc93781c1947b53cff50a550ad551e462a464594` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6e2cd4e2d5d79aef349154d5059207a79b4bfab0` — the merge of head `20c00221c6ff0a2a41e1d94f9396f69dd831fb23` into base `dc93781c1947b53cff50a550ad551e462a464594`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6e2cd4e2d5d79aef349154d5059207a79b4bfab0 && git checkout 6e2cd4e2d5d79aef349154d5059207a79b4bfab0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dc93781c1947b53cff50a550ad551e462a464594 20c00221c6ff0a2a41e1d94f9396f69dd831fb23 && git checkout -B drift-repro dc93781c1947b53cff50a550ad551e462a464594 && git merge --no-ff 20c00221c6ff0a2a41e1d94f9396f69dd831fb23

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dc93781c1947b53cff50a550ad551e462a464594
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dc93781c1947b53cff50a550ad551e462a464594` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f88009a41844019b524ba71124ece3d30ba83a36`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23026 (body and all five comments, the `os-dev-report` and the seat's ACCEPT included), PR #23140 (body, the six-file list, the net diff against `main` at this head), the 39 check-runs on the head, `origin/main` at `1ca7a805ca` and the head fetched into a private ref — all read-only. Judged independently of the seat's ACCEPT; where I agree with it, I say what I read, not that it said so.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`component-props-invalid` files a `retiredKey()` tombstone verdict as `error` — RIGHT, and the refused class is exactly the tombstone class.** `isTombstoneIssue` reads `code === 'invalid_type'` and `expected === 'never'`, the same discriminator as the spec's own `isRetiredKeyIssue` (`automation/flow-node-config-refusals.ts:459`). I enumerated every `never`-producing construct reachable from `ComponentPropsMap` on the head: 38 `retiredKey()` sites in `ui/component.zod.ts` (`page:header` `icon` / `breadcrumb`, `page:tabs` `type`, `page:card` `actions` / `body`, `record:details` `layout`, the ten flat binding keys of `element:number` / `element:record_picker` / `element:repeater`, the six keys of `element:filter`, the six of `element:form`, three `targetVariable`s, `displayField`, `searchFields`, `multiple`, `object-grid` `defaultFilters` / `defaultSort` / `resizableColumns`, `object-kanban` `quickAdd`, `details[].sortField`); three more through imports (`NavigationConfigSchema.view`, `FormFieldSchema.publicPicker`, `ChartConfigSchema.aria` by way of `ReportSchema.extend`); and the two `retiredComponentProps` rows (`user:profile`, `ai:chat_window`). Nothing else reachable raises `expected: 'never'`: `strictObject()` is `z.object(...).strict()` and zod 4 folds a `never` catchall into `unrecognized_keys` (the measured note at `view.zod.ts:6806-6817`; the PR's `titel` pin holds it); `enumWithRetiredValues` is a `z.enum`, so a retired value is an enum issue; the one hand-built `invalid_type` in the UI graph (`view.zod.ts:6779`) carries `expected: 'object'`; the non-tombstone `z.never().optional()` on `ViewItemWireSchema.options` (`view.zod.ts:5663`) is unreachable — `component.zod.ts` references no ViewItem schema and takes `ListViewSchema` members by `.shape` pick only; the `viewItems` and inline-credential nevers sit on the stack and driver schemas. No `expected: 'never'` literal exists in spec source outside comments, so nothing hand-built can spoof the shape.
2. **The union-arm rule** (`invalid_union` whose arms contain exactly one all-tombstone arm) — RIGHT and conservative. It mirrors `unrecognizedKeysFromUnionArm`, which runs first in the loop, so a union where another arm judged keys routes to the unknown-key warning and never reaches the classifier. Live on one shape (`sections[].fields[]`, `publicPicker`); the mixed-arm case is pinned a warning.
3. **Every other finding stays a `warning`** — RIGHT at the rule (the other branches of the loop are untouched) and at the doors: `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` partition by `splitBySeverity` on `severity === 'error'`; `tier` is read by no runtime path, only by `authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts`, which forces the `advisory` → `gating` flip for any rule that emits `error`. The #23076 url `target` and #23080 section `count` refusals, a retired enum value, an undeclared key and the missing `dataSource.object` binding remain warnings, each pinned.
4. **`ComponentPropsSeverity` widens to `'error' | 'warning'`** — a public type of `@objectstack/lint`; RIGHT to ride the `major`.
5. **The retired element rows become an `error` from this rule** — declared in the changeset; RIGHT, and it opens no new door-level refusal: `PageComponentSchema.type` already refuses a retired type at the parse (`page.zod.ts:557-574`), so the row is reachable only by calling the rule directly. One wording note: the hint's "keeps a retired key only to refuse it" is loose for a whole-bag `z.never` row; unreachable through the doors, so a note, not a defect.
6. **Rule header, message and hint — TRUE.** "The prescription above" holds in both shapes: `describeIssue` prints a tombstone's `message` directly and, for a collapsed union, every arm's issues with their messages.
7. **The two edited registry sentences** (`registry.ts:5135-5139`, `:9822-9824`) — TRUE on the head: the load path keeps the open `properties` bag; the three CLI doors refuse; `os migrate meta` lists the edits.
8. **WRONG — two further registry sentences the diff falsifies and does not touch.** `registry.ts:10612-10613` (`page-header-breadcrumb-removed`: "The tombstone on `PageHeaderProps` refuses it for a live author (advisory, via the props lint ...)") and `:13554-13555` (`object-master-detail-form-detail-sort-field-removed`: "The tombstone refuses the key for a live author (advisory, via the props lint ...)"). Both keys are `retiredKey()` tombstones this head files as `error` — the PR's own flipped pins at `validate-component-props.test.ts:90` and `:116` prove it. The ADR-0087 ledger now says "refuse" at `:5137` and "advisory" at `:10612` about one gate. This is the card's own defect class — registry text misdescribing what the props gate does — introduced in the file the amended claim covers; the PR body's "two sentences, no other region of the file" was a sweep that stopped at the two sentences the card cited. Not shipped (`registry.ts` is outside spec's `files` glob and both consts are unexported), so no consumer reads it; the ledger's maintainers do, and the `spec-property-retirement` playbook models the next retirement on these entries.
9. Pre-existing, out of scope, to file: `registry.ts:8327-8328` (`element-text-variant-heading-subheading-retired`) says "an author is refused at parse with the prescription" — `element:text.variant` is an `enumWithRetiredValues` value verdict, a props-gate WARNING before and after this PR; its own D3 entry (`migrations/entries/semantic/18.element-text-variant-heading-subheading-retired.ts:36`) says advisory, correctly. Same class as the card, not this PR's doing. The comment at `migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__PageHeaderProps__breadcrumb.ts:17` ("parsed only by the advisory props lint, which writes nothing back") belongs in the same sweep; the residue point it makes stays true.
10. **Could a test or gate pass while the classification is wrong?** Not in the direction that matters. The schema-graph pin (every top-level `optional(never)` in the map must file an `error` at its own key, anti-vacuity floor of 30 plus the specimen) reds if any tombstone stops classifying; the direct, union, mixed-union, per-issue and four stays-a-warning pins red on over-reach; the pipeline pin reds if `runAuthoringRules` drops the error. The dev's two ablations (9 reds, then 1, exactly the expected pins) read the same way. Check-runs on the head at read time: 26 success (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Type Check · source gates` / `consumer gates` / `debt ledger`, `Spec property liveness` among them), 6 skipped (full-battery jobs), 7 in progress (`Test Core` 1–6/6, `Type Check · workspace`). No governed surface in the file list; 384 changed lines; same-repo head; draft.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/lint: major` — RIGHT.** `(narrowing)` is BREAKING. `.changeset/pre.json` is `mode: pre`, tag `next`, so `check-changeset-no-major`'s RC exemption admits a `major`, and the fixed group already carries many pending majors (`22130-protocol-18.md` among them), so this adds no release level. House precedent for this very gate is `11509-element-flat-binding-retired.md` (`@objectstack/lint: major`). The lockstep group bumps `@objectstack/cli` with it; the sentence belongs in lint's CHANGELOG, where the refusal text lives — a CLI line is not owed. `@objectstack/spec` publishes nothing from this diff (a docblock on unexported consts, one test exclusion), so no spec line is owed and `skip-changeset` does not apply to a published package.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — RIGHT**, present in both carriers (PR body line 2, verbatim from the claim; changeset body). The level axis is not engaged.
- **ADR-0087 marker — RIGHT.** Exactly one marker, the `**BREAKING**` token present, `not-required (already-registered ...)` in the ADR's grammar. The gate verifies only that the 20 ids resolve and pre-date the base (ADR-0087 says coverage is the author's honesty), so I checked coverage by hand: the 38 in-file tombstones and the three imported ones all map onto the 20 ids (`page-structure-inert-keys-removed` covers `page:header.icon` / `page:card.actions`; `element-flat-data-binding-to-data-source` the ten flat keys; `record-picker-inert-keys-removed` `searchFields` / `multiple`; `element-input-target-variable-removed` the three `targetVariable`s; `element-filter-removed` / `element-form-removed` the two retired elements' key rows; `list-view-navigation-view-retired`, `form-field-public-picker-retired`, `chart-config-aria-retired`, `ui-ai-chat-window-retired` the rest). "Every key this refuses ... with its ledger entry" is true of every key; `user:profile` is an element with no ledger id of its own, but it is refused at the parse already (①.5), so nothing newly refused lacks an entry. The diff adds no entry and amends none, so `registered` would be false data; `already-registered` is the honest disposition.
- **Changeset body — TRUE.** "What is refused" and "What stays a warning" match `isRetiredKeyVerdict` and the loop; "Not judged here" matches `surfaces: CLI_ONLY` (`authoring-rules.ts:1194`) and the open bag; the FROM → TO rows match the `defaultFilters` conversion's precedence and `record-picker-display-field-to-label-field`; "0 newly refused" is the dev's measurement over the four examples and the five shipped pages with a lit positive control, and no example or template changed in the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **File surface (dev deviation; the seat amended the claim) — RIGHT disposition.** `authoring-rules.ts` (tier flip) is forced by the wiring test; `form-field-public-picker-retirement.test.ts` (one EXCLUDED entry) is forced by the tree-scoped absence pin, the pattern the breadcrumb and sortField pins already use; `registry.ts` — the dispatch pre-authorized the two sentences only on the fallback branch, but both were false under either branch (no branch makes the loader refuse), so correcting them beside the severity change is right. That amendment is also what makes ①.8 a defect of this PR rather than a note: the claim now covers registry sentences about this gate's refusal, and two were left contradicting it.
- **Resume, background build, env listing, commit trailers — answered.** The env listing predates the rule and printed names only; the four commits carry the model-free trailer pair (read in the branch log); no model identifier in title, body, changeset or comments.
- **`open_questions` (class (b) to `error`?) → option A, filed #23147 — RIGHT.** B abandons the header's recorded plan; C stages without external evidence; A measures an external corpus first, which the in-repo zero cannot stand in for.
- **Out-of-scope 1 (tombstone text says "removed in @objectstack/spec 17" for keys live in 17.7.0) → filed #23145 — RIGHT carrier** (spec text, its own pins). One thing worth saying on that card: this PR turns that string from a warning into the error text an author is stopped on, so it is more urgent than it was.
- **Out-of-scope 2 (two stale sibling test comments) → acceptance notes, carrier none — acceptable** for test comments; the same sweep owed the registry docblocks (①.8) and the two sibling sites in ①.9.
- **Out-of-scope 3 (`surfaceReason: RUNTIME_NEEDS_FULL_SNAPSHOT` looks inaccurate for a page-local rule; the runtime publish door does not run a now-gating rule) → carrier none — ESCALATE.** The changeset keeps the claim as narrow as the enforcement, which is why this is not a FAIL cause; but a gating CLI rule the Studio / REST / MCP door does not run, declared under a reason the dev believes wrong, is a decision the rules say must be made (measure the page-write snapshot; decide the runtime-door rollout with its false-refusal budget), not an acceptance note. The owning seat should file it.
- **Seat pointer 6129214439 (#23076 url `target`, #23080 section `count`) — answered in the diff:** both stay warnings, both pinned.

**Why FAIL, and what lifts it.** The narrowing, its severity, its doors, the changeset and the marker are right in every respect I could derive, and no shipped sentence is false. The head fails on the contract path leg alone: the diff falsifies `registry.ts:10612-10613` and `:13554-13555` and leaves them, so the ADR-0087 ledger describes one gate as refusing at `:5137` and advisory at `:10612`. Remedy: rewrite those two parentheticals to say the props lint refuses the key as an `error` at `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` (the load path keeps the open bag); sweep `registry.ts` and `migrations/entries` for any other tier claim about a tombstone's props-gate finding (`:8327-8328` is a pre-existing one of the sibling class — file it, or fold it under the amended claim); push. A record on that head can take ① and ② above as read.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23026-retired-prop-error`
Reviewed-by: `session_012uFegdfR6K6uqvLzt7XsdZ`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `175a546b8cdc7c148d79cd77ad5154565828820f`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23026 (body and all nine comments: triage, the claim, the seat pointer, three `os-dev-report`s, the ACCEPT and the two amendments), PR #23140 (body, the nine-file list, the net diff against `main` at this head), the two PR comments (the docs-drift notice and the FAIL record 6137697373 on `f88009a41`), the 46 check-runs on this head, `origin/main` at `02bec6ca86`, the head fetched into a private ref, the `@objectstack/lint@17.7.0` tag, and `git diff f88009a41..175a546b8` — all read-only. The seat's ACCEPT and amendments were tested, not adopted; where I agree, I say what I read.

**How far the head moved.** Two commits since `f88009a41` (`f1905ac90`, `175a546b8`): four files, +32/−15. Every changed line in `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts` (23 added, 9 removed) and in `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__PageHeaderProps__breadcrumb.ts` (3 added, 2 removed) is a ` * ` or `// ` comment line — counted mechanically over the diff — plus two `content/docs/**` pages. No code, test, changeset or `packages/lint` line moved, so the rule, the doors, the classifier and the changeset are byte-identical to what record 6137697373 judged. Both commits carry the model-free trailer pair; no model identifier in title, body, changeset, comments or commits.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Carried by reference from 6137697373 ①.1–①.6 and ①.10** — the code they judge did not move. I re-read the load-bearing points on this head rather than only trusting them: `isTombstoneIssue` reads `invalid_type` with `expected === 'never'`, the spec's own `isRetiredKeyIssue` discriminator (`automation/flow-node-config-refusals.ts:459-461`); `retiredKey()` is `z.never(...).optional()` (`shared/retired-key.ts:186`), 42 sites in `ui/component.zod.ts` plus the two `retiredComponentProps` rows; in the dispatch loop (`validate-component-props.ts:286-447`) the walker's unknown keys, a union arm's and a strict row's `unrecognized_keys`, the missing `dataSource.object` binding and every non-tombstone value verdict are `warning`, and only `isRetiredKeyVerdict` files `error`; an unregistered type is skipped at `:303`. `splitBySeverity` (`authoring-rules.ts:2252`) partitions on `severity === 'error'`, and `cli/src/utils/author-time-rules.ts:146-149` turns a non-empty error set into the refusal `os validate`, `os build` and `os lint` exit on; the registry entry is `tier: 'gating'`, `commands: ALL`, `surfaces: CLI_ONLY`. The refused class is exactly the tombstone class and nothing wider: `enumWithRetiredValues` returns `z.enum(values, { error })` (`retired-key.ts:422-437`), an enum issue; every `filter` door is `z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema, { error: ruleArrayFilterError(...) })` (`component.zod.ts:5254` and its siblings), so a legacy record there is `invalid_type` expecting `array`, a warning; a `time` default's zone refusal reaches an inline action through `valueSchemaFor(def, 'stored').safeParse` inside a refinement (`data/default-value-shape.ts:181`), never a `never`. "Could a test or gate pass while the classification is wrong?" — no: the schema-graph pin (every `optional(never)` in the map must file an `error` at its own key, anti-vacuity floor 30) and the four stays-a-warning pins bracket the class from both sides, and nothing in this head moved them.
2. **The FAIL's remedy on `registry.ts:10621-10625` and `:13565-13569` — RIGHT and TRUE.** `breadcrumb` (`component.zod.ts:660`) and `details[].sortField` (`:8336`) are `retiredKey()` tombstones; both docblocks now say the three CLI doors refuse the key as an `error` with the prescription via the component-props gate, and that the load path keeps the open `properties` bag as written. Both halves hold: `PageComponentSchema.properties` is the open bag, parsed by no load-path schema. The ledger no longer calls one gate "refuse" at `:5137` and "advisory" at `:10622`.
3. **The three folded-in registry sentences — TRUE on the head.** `:5836-5839` (`page-tabs-type-to-tab-style`): `page:tabs` `type` is `retiredKey()` (`component.zod.ts:794`), an `error` at the three doors, and `tsc` still refuses it at the authoring site. `:8333-8340` (`element-text-variant-heading-levels`): `element:text` `variant` is `enumWithRetiredValues` (`:2980`), so an old spelling is an enum issue and stays a `warning`, which is what the sentence now says. `:8032-8037` (`time-default-utc-suffix-dropped`): on an `element:button` the inline action sits in the open bag and the refinement's issue is a `warning` from this rule — TRUE; the untouched `objects[]` / `actions[]` half ("refused at parse") predates this PR, is not a props-gate sentence, and I did not measure it beyond the stack schema parsing those arrays — NOT MEASURED, as the dev recorded. `:5135-5139` and `:9830-9832`, the first round's two edits, remain TRUE (`displayField` / `searchFields` / `multiple` at `component.zod.ts:3571-3594` and `defaultFilters` at `:5278` are all `retiredKey()`).
4. **`retired-keys/18.ui__PageHeaderProps__breadcrumb.ts:16-19` — TRUE as dated.** At the `@objectstack/lint@17.7.0` tag the rule is `tier: 'advisory'` and `ComponentPropsSeverity = 'warning'` is a single literal, and `breadcrumb` is already a tombstone there, so every release that shipped the `.default(true)` shipped an advisory props lint; the lint writes nothing back. The residue argument stands.
